thread.document:
EECS 182 Special Participation E - Graph Explorer!

Website: https://182-e-graphs.vercel.app/

Github: https://github.com/deenasun/182-participation-e-graphs

Team: Deena Sun, Eric Wang, Celine Tan, and Tvisha Londe

The graph explorer home page!

Filtering the graph to show a selected cluster's nodes and edges.

Expandable sidebar with additional post details, student, date, and attachments.

Project Summary

We built an interactive graph-based website that transforms Special Participation E submissions (AI-enhanced learning tools created by EECS 182 students) from a linear EdStem feed into a searchable, semantically-organized network. Instead of scrolling through hundreds of posts, students and course staff can visually explore relationships between submissions, discover similar tools, and gain visibility for their work through an intuitive force-directed graph visualization.

The project addresses the challenge of discovering and navigating 200+ student participation posts scattered across EdStem. Traditional forum interfaces make it difficult to find related content, understand thematic connections, or explore tools by category. Our solution uses graph visualization and machine learning to surface semantic relationships, enabling users to explore posts by topic similarity, tool type, or LLM used—transforming a flat list into an interactive knowledge network.

Features

Interactive Graph Visualization

Force-directed 2D graph powered by D3.js physics simulation: each node represents a student post and edges indicate semantic similarity and thematic relationships based on different view modes (see below!)

Distinct view modes: the graph supports 3 ways of classifying and clustering nodes

Topic View: Semantic clusters using BERTopic topic modeling (e.g., "transformer", "neural network", "reinforcement learning")

Tool View: Grouped by tool types (flashcard, quiz, interactive visualization, diagram, notebook, chat, summary)

LLM View: Organized by LLMs used (GPT, Claude, Gemini, NotebookLM, Perplexity, Other)

After selecting a view mode, you can also filter by the different labels in each mode to highlight nodes in the graph belonging to that cluster

Clusters are color-coded to visually distinguish groups from one another

Node sizing represents the "impressiveness score" of a post---calculated based on engagement metrics, content length, and attachment presence as a way to approximate Professor Ranade's request: If you think some submissions are particularly impressive, highlight them. :)

Real-Time Search & Discovery

Hybrid search combining keyword matching (PostgreSQL full-text search) and semantic similarity (vector embeddings via pgvector)

Search result highlighting that instantly highlights matching nodes in red on the graph

Search by user, content, date, or post number!

Post Detail Sidebar

Click-to-explore workflow: click any graph node to open a detailed sidebar

The sidebar includes:

Full post content with formatted text display

Category tags showing extracted topics, tools, and LLMs with color-coded badges

Student attribution with extracted links to GitHub repositories, personal websites, and LinkedIn profiles

Attachment access with PDF text extraction summaries (first 3 pages, up to 5000 characters)

Deep-Learning Concepts Used

Our system leverages several deep learning techniques to extract semantic meaning and organize content.

Sentence Transformers (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) generates 384-dimensional embeddings using transformer-based neural networks, capturing semantic relationships between posts.

BERTopic performs unsupervised topic modeling, discovering latent themes through transformer embeddings.

UMAP reduces high-dimensional embeddings to 2D coordinates while preserving structure, and HDBSCAN identifies natural clusters in the reduced space.

Implementation

Implementation Details - Category-Aware Embeddings

We think our core innovation is generating view-specific embeddings that fuse content with category information. Each post has four embedding vectors:

Base content_embedding for general semantic search

topic_view_embedding (content + topic labels, weighted 60/40)

tool_view_embedding (content + tool types, weighted 60/40)

llm_view_embedding (content + LLM names, weighted 60/40)

This ensures each view mode produces meaningfully different clusters—switching from Topic to Tool View reorganizes the graph rather than just recoloring it.


Implementation Details - Graph Layout Computation

We pre-computed layouts using UMAP (dimensionality reduction) and HDBSCAN (clustering) for each view mode. Positions are stored in the database to enable instant view switching without recomputation. Edge similarities are pre-calculated using cosine similarity on view-specific embeddings, with top-k connections (k=5) above a 0.6 threshold.

Implementation Details - Data Ingestion Pipeline

Our backend includes an automated ingestion pipeline that:

Fetches posts from EdStem API (or processes JSON exports)

Extracts text from PDF attachments (PyPDF2)

Trains BERTopic model on all post content for topic discovery

Categorizes posts using keyword matching (tools, LLMs) and BERTopic (topics)

Generates embeddings using Sentence-Transformers (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, 384-dim)

Computes graph layouts and similarity edges for all three view modes

Stores everything in Supabase with pgvector for fast similarity search

Backend Architecture

FastAPI REST API with 10+ endpoints for graph data, posts, search, and admin functions

Supabase (PostgreSQL + pgvector) for vector similarity search and relational data

Python ingestion pipeline with modular components (embedder, categorizer, graph_builder, pdf_processor)

Frontend Architecture

React18 with TypeScript for type safety

react-force-graph-2d for D3.js-powered graph visualization

@tanstack/react-query for efficient data fetching and caching

Tailwind CSS for responsive, modern UI

Component-based architecture (Graph, Sidebar, SearchBar, CategoryToggle)

Deployment

Backend deployed on Render

Frontend deployed on Vercel

Data stored on Supabase

Current Data Collected:

249 posts processed and visualized

1,376 similarity edges connecting related posts

Multiple tool categories: flashcard, quiz, interactive, diagram, notebook, chat, summary

6+ LLM providers: GPT, Claude, Gemini, NotebookLM, Perplexity, Other

BERTopic-generated topics with semantic clustering

PDF attachments extracted and summarized for enhanced searchability

comments.content: <document version="2.0"><paragraph>This graph visualization is nice! Made me think about the posts in a different way than I had before. Do you think it might be easy to integrate the visualiztion part into a different teams website --- I'm thinking if it is possible to combine the best features of all the websites together...</paragraph></document>
comments.document: This graph visualization is nice! Made me think about the posts in a different way than I had before. Do you think it might be easy to integrate the visualiztion part into a different teams website --- I'm thinking if it is possible to combine the best features of all the websites together...

comments.content: <document version="2.0"><paragraph>Hi Professor Ranade, thank you for checking our website out! It should be definitely doable to include our graph visualizations as part of a wider website–I foresee the main requirements while merging to be implementing the endpoints in the backend to fetch the data for the graph, setting up connections with our database, and refactoring the graph components into a self-contained tab/subpage. All the components we built are modular and should be flexible enough to plug and play as needed :)</paragraph></document>
comments.document: Hi Professor Ranade, thank you for checking our website out! It should be definitely doable to include our graph visualizations as part of a wider website–I foresee the main requirements while merging to be implementing the endpoints in the backend to fetch the data for the graph, setting up connections with our database, and refactoring the graph components into a self-contained tab/subpage. All the components we built are modular and should be flexible enough to plug and play as needed :)
